finding: The live range starts too low and tops out slightly low for V8 trucks. Our implied totals (parts + hours x $120-$160/hr) are: economy $2,397-$3,301, midsize $2,364-$3,204, truck (both heads) $2,686-$4,445; luxury could not be totalled because no stated labor time was found for the BMW N20 (parts alone $274-$407). Nothing we could build from real parts prices and stated book times comes near the live low of $1,075: on these modern engines the book time is 17-25 hours, so labor alone is about $2,000-$4,000. RepairPal ($2,572-$3,386 national) and CarParts.com ($2,400-$3,200) agree with our numbers; only a 2023 J.D. Power article ($1,000-$3,000) supports the low end, and RepairPal's Silverado 1500 figure ($1,989-$2,544) shows simpler pushrod V8s can be cheaper. A floor near $2,000-$2,300 and a ceiling near $4,400-$4,600 would fit the evidence better. Caveats: the economy and midsize hours rest partly on a labor-time site that does not state its source (corroborated by an Alldata figure for a sister engine and a CarParts.com statement); the midsize parts figure is a single aftermarket set price without head bolts; the truck bolt-set listing does not say whether it covers both heads; fluids (coolant, oil, filter) were not priced and are not in the parts figures.
extras: Machine-shop work is the biggest add-on: the head is normally checked for flatness and cracks and resurfaced, and a warped or cracked head means more machining or a replacement head. Quotes also commonly add coolant, engine oil and filter, thermostat, spark plugs, a diagnosis fee (cooling-system pressure test or combustion-gas test), shop supplies and sales tax. Many shops recommend doing the timing chain or belt, water pump and related seals while the engine is apart, and V engines may be quoted for one head or both, so check which the quote covers.
